body:
A machine check that sets up the graphics card, Find a model, the OpenAI platform as its own upstream, Anthropic's blocks carried natively, image and audio tools in the Chat, and the Chat as a crate other apps can host.

- **The machine check.** At start lmgw checks whether this computer can run local models and says what is missing in plain words: the graphics card and its driver (Secure Boot included, amdgpu on AMD), NVIDIA's container toolkit, Podman, the model settings against the card, free space and the engine downloads. It shows as the "This computer" card first in **Settings → GPU**, as a card on the Overview and above the Chat's empty state, and as a banner in the Chat while local models are involved (a cloud-only setup is not nagged; "Not now" quiets all three). The tray adds **Graphics card needs attention…** when the verdict leaves ready.
  - **Set it up** installs the toolkit through a fixed root helper, `/usr/libexec/lmgw/lmgw-machine-helper`, behind lmgw's own confirmation (every command and file under "Show the commands") and one polkit password prompt. It runs only from the app's window and as a system task (`lmgw-machine-setup.service`), so closing lmgw doesn't interrupt it. Where the helper can't apply (no dnf, an image-based system) the check lists the commands to type instead.
  - lmgw writes the card's CDI description itself, without root, into its own runtime directory, rewrites it after a driver or package update and passes it to its containers with `--cdi-spec-dir`; there is no `nvidia-ctk cdi generate` to run for them.
  - Model settings made for the other vendor's card (AMD Vulkan or NVIDIA CUDA) can be switched in one confirmed step, with every change listed.
  - A start the computer can't make answers `503 gpu_setup` with the reason, or the model's fallback answers it. The check and its fix are also the `machine_check` op and the `lmgw__machine_check` tool.
- **Engine images arrive with the model.** A model download also fetches the image its class runs in, and a start whose image is missing downloads it before admission, showing its bytes, without taking a place in the queue. A failed image download answers `engine_download`.
- **Find a model.** **Models → Find a model** takes a name as someone said it ("qwen 3.6") or any Hugging Face link, searches the hub live (originals before uploads, no model list of lmgw's own) and answers one card: the original, the upload and the file that fits this machine's card, judged by the listed sizes and then a Range read of the GGUF header, before anything downloads. **Get it** downloads the file with its companions, plans it, fits its context to the card and creates the row without starting it; **Say hello** opens a thread. **Send to a friend** copies the model's name and its public Hugging Face address, and a pasted share text plans that exact file. **Add from Hugging Face** marks every file by its fit and preselects the recommended one. Self-admin agents get `lmgw__model_find`, `lmgw__model_get` and `lmgw__model_get_status`.
  - Downloads resume from their `.part` after a restart, are checked by length and sha256 before they are renamed into place, and pause on a metered connection.
  - A fresh install needs no settings to download: it keeps models under `~/.local/share/lmgw/models/`, one folder per class, shown and changed under **Settings → Runtimes**.
- **Binary units everywhere.** Every byte figure lmgw shows or says (the machine check, downloads, image pulls, disk, card memory, body sizes, notes, tool sentences) is in KiB, MiB, GiB or TiB, through one formatter.
- **The OpenAI platform gets its own egress.** The `openai` protocol now means api.openai.com only; every other OpenAI-shaped provider is `openai_compatible`.
  - `/v1/responses` goes to the platform natively, metered and priced, unless only lmgw's loop can serve the request (an MCP label lmgw serves, a `previous_response_id` lmgw stored). Hosted tools pass through on the native path. Stored responses belong to the key that made them, and `GET`/`DELETE`/`input_items` on a native id go through its upstream.
  - Chat sends to the platform go over the Responses API unless they set `stop`, `seed`, a penalty or carry audio. Encrypted reasoning survives across turns: in the Chat, as a thinking block's `signature` on `/v1/messages` and as `encrypted_content` on `/v1/responses`. A model's refusal is its own part.
  - **Service tiers.** lmgw asks for `service_tier: auto` when the client set none and prices each answer at the tier it reports. Price rows have a tier; traffic at a tier with no price stays unpriced with a note, and the Prices page lists it.
  - **Budget floors.** A tier with no price, or a stream cut before its usage, still counts against budgets at a floor (the standard price, or a local token count). A budgeted caller is refused with `budget_unpriced` on a model with no price for what it is billed in, flex without a flex price included.
  - `max_completion_tokens` for the output cap; llama.cpp samplers are left out and named in `x-lmgw-params-ignored`; OpenRouter's `reasoning` object becomes `reasoning_effort`; OpenAI's error codes, `Retry-After` and `x-ratelimit-*` reach the client.
- **One fallback per model and alias.** Every model and alias has one **Fallback** setting, used for every reason it can't answer: the GPU hold, a benchmark, VRAM taken outside lmgw, a deferred background request, a card that isn't set up, an exhausted quota, an unreachable upstream or a disabled row. A fallback is served as if the client had named it, so it can hand on to its own; `x-lmgw-fallback-chain` lists each hop with its reason. A fallback must be of the same model type and may be a local model; a loop is refused. lmgw remembers an upstream that is out of quota and skips straight to its fallback until a re-check (`quota_recheck_seconds`, under Usage & cost) or **Check now**.
- **Anthropic, natively.** Between a Messages client and an Anthropic upstream, lmgw now carries what it used to flatten, whole and streamed: thinking blocks with their signatures, blocks it doesn't model (`redacted_thinking`, server tool blocks, newer types) verbatim, text block citations, compaction blocks and `context_management` edits, and Files API sources for images and documents. Every other route gets the nearest equivalent (the compaction summary as text, citations dropped) and `x-lmgw-params-ignored` names what was left out. Signed and verbatim blocks go back only to the upstream that produced them. The Anthropic dialect of `/v1/models` carries Anthropic's capability blocks.
- **Stalled streams end.** An upstream that stays silent past its timeout ends the client's stream with the protocol's own error. Keep-alive comments only hold a stream open while the model may be thinking out of sight or a provider-run tool is running.
- **Structured output, translated everywhere.** `response_format`, `text.format` and `output_config.format` are one field that every egress writes in its upstream's form (Anthropic `output_config.format`, Gemini `responseJsonSchema`). A model whose capabilities say it can't is refused early with `response_format_unsupported`; upstream schema refusals arrive as `invalid_json_schema` or `response_format_unsupported` with `param`.
- **Image and audio tools for the Chat.** `image__generate`, `image__edit`, `image__upscale`, `audio__speak` and `audio__transcribe` are a built-in toolset on `/mcp` and, in Chat threads, the labels `image` and `audio`. A running call shows its stage, step progress and previews and can be cancelled. A generated picture gets a card with Re-roll, Vary, Edit and Upscale that work without the chat model (`POST /chat/api/attachments/{id}/media`). Default models per tool are set in **Settings → Chat**, a folder or a thread.
- **The Chat on the Chat plane.** The dashboard's Chat reads only `/chat/api/*` and `/v1` routes, scoped to the caller (new reads for its settings, toolsets, tools and knowledge bases), and is a crate of its own, `lmgw-chat-ui`, with a narrow layout down to 280 px and no inline scripts, so a paired device can host the same Chat. Kai for Firefox shows it in a Firefox sidebar.
  - A message can carry its `origin`, where the user writes from, kept out of the system prompt.
  - Conversations can be renamed (menu or F2; `POST /chat/api/threads/{id}/title`), New chat starts in the open thread's folder, the composer is one input bubble, and side panels can be dragged wider or narrower.
- **Device-to-device transfers.** A paired device can offer a file to another device of the same app (an app id declared at pairing), relayed through lmgw: a resumable ranged upload checked by sha256 (`/transfers/api/transfers`), the offer on the Chat feed as `transfer.updated`, a ranged download, and expiry. The Devices card gets a Transfers section, and enrolment carries the device's own name.
- **API compatibility checks.** Every gate run checks each body lmgw sends upstream and each `/v1` answer and stream event against OpenAI's OpenAPI spec, Anthropic's SDK schemas and Gemini's discovery document. `scripts/compat-live.sh` drives multi-turn scenarios through the official SDKs against a running lmgw; its results are published at https://lmgw-dev.github.io/docs/compat/. New on the way: `POST /v1/responses/input_tokens`, and a sampling parameter a model refuses is retried once without it, left out from then on and named in `x-lmgw-params-refused`.
- **Background requests.** `x-lmgw-background: on` makes one request a guest on the GPU: it uses a local model only where that disturbs nobody, otherwise the fallback answers or a `503 gpu_deferred` says to retry. The Models page shows a model's deferrals over the last 24 hours.
- **The Voices lab.** Under Labs: rounds of candidate voice samples from any text-to-speech alias, saved to the voice library with their exact transcript (also `lmgw__voice_generate`, `lmgw__voice_sample_save`).
- **Audio.** `/v1/audio/alignments` answers one typed shape whatever model aligned (seconds, the sample rate, each word's character span in the submitted transcript), and every local audio row publishes its languages.
- **Dashboard.** Engine builds and images are **Engines** (Overview's section is **Running models**); the sidebar nests Labs and Downloads; messages name settings by their labels (**Settings → GPU → Admission → Load timeout**), not config keys; the window remembers its size.

**Breaking / upgrade notes**

- **Clients:** Kai 0.3.0, Kai mobile 0.2.0 and Kai for Firefox 0.1.0 are the releases built against this one; older Kai builds pin lmgw 0.5.0.
- **`openai` rows become `openai_compatible`** (migration 0090), whatever their host, and the start notice names each one. Switch an api.openai.com row back to `openai` on the Upstreams page to get the platform egress. `supports_responses` is an `openai_compatible` choice only and is cleared on Anthropic and Gemini rows; `audio_cpp` rows must be `openai_compatible`.
- **The global hold fallback and `inherit` are gone** (migration 0095). Each row keeps the fallback it answered with, the start notice names the rows whose fallback came from the global, and a fallback of another model type is refused at the row's next save.
- **Budgets count only what is priced in full:** a budgeted caller is refused on models with no price for what they bill (a price of 0 is allowed).
- **Answers changed:** an upstream 503 is `502 api_error` (only a 529 is `overloaded_error`); rate and quota refusals carry OpenAI's own code and type, an exhausted quota on `/v1/messages` is `402 billing_error`, and an OpenAI 4xx lmgw has no word for is relayed as sent; `languages` moved from `capabilities.speech` to the top of `capabilities`; `/v1/audio/alignments` is lmgw's typed shape, no longer audio.cpp's JSON. New codes: `gpu_setup`, `engine_download`, `budget_unpriced`.
- **A silent upstream now ends a stream** after its timeout, where keep-alive comments used to hold it open.
- Migrations 0085 to 0100 run on start. The RPM depends on `polkit` and ships the root helper and its polkit action (`io.github.lmgw-dev.lmgw.machine-setup`); building the RPM by hand needs `cargo build --release -p lmgw-machine-helper` before `cargo tauri build`, as `ci/build.sh` does.

**Fixes**

- Every answer from the gateway's origin except the dashboard's own sends `nosniff` and `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox`, so stored or relayed content can't run as the dashboard.
- The updater runs `pkexec` and `dnf` by absolute path and downloads the RPM into a private directory instead of a fixed `/tmp` path.
- The RPM no longer ships group- or world-writable files.
- A streamed chat stops its model as soon as the client goes, even while the model is prefilling.
- A split GGUF is charged for every part, not only the first.
- A tool call with no arguments goes upstream as `{}`; an MP3's `input_audio` goes as `mp3`; the `/v1` answers carry the fields OpenAI's and Anthropic's schemas require (`logprobs: null` and others).
- Chat attachments, lab files and voice clips answer `Range` requests with `206`.
name: lmgw 0.6.0

body:
Realtime voice over WebRTC, an encrypted and mutually authenticated link for paired devices, decision models, and labs that keep their history. lmgw is MIT-licensed from this release.

- **WebRTC realtime calls.** `POST /v1/realtime/calls` is OpenAI's WebRTC transport for `/v1/realtime` sessions, in OpenAI's shape: post an SDP offer (raw `application/sdp`, or multipart with a `session` part) with your key and get the answer back. Audio is Opus over UDP, encrypted with DTLS-SRTP; events travel on the `oai-events` data channel; `POST /v1/realtime/calls/{call_id}/hangup` ends a call. OpenAI's browser example and the Agents SDK's `OpenAIRealtimeWebRTC` work with the base URL pointed at lmgw. lmgw answers as ICE-lite with one host candidate, the address the POST arrived on, and has no STUN or TURN: the client must reach that address directly, on the LAN or through a VPN. The UDP port is the HTTP port's number unless **Settings → Realtime → WebRTC calls** names another; that group also lists the live calls.
- **The device link.** Paired devices connect to a TLS listener of their own and authenticate with a certificate; bearer device keys are gone. The plain listener stays HTTP for local OpenAI clients and the dashboard.
  - lmgw runs a small private CA. The pairing QR code or link carries the CA's fingerprint, a one-time token and the URLs to try (LAN, VPN). The device makes its own key, enrols the public half with the token and gets a certificate, and both sides check each other from then on.
  - Each enrolment is confirmed on the **Devices** card: the device and the card show the same short code, and the device opens nothing until you click Confirm. The card also copies the CA certificate and rotates the CA. The CA's key is encrypted under the desktop's Secret Service.
  - The listener is off until you pair a device; the pairing form offers to turn it on and, for another machine, to widen it. Its port is the HTTP port's number plus one (**Settings → Network & access → Devices**).
- **The Chat feed is a push channel for devices.** `GET /chat/api/feed` takes `keepalive_s` (up to `chat_feed_keepalive_max_s`, default 900), so a phone can hold the connection open in the background. `hello` carries the keep-alive, the device's URLs, certificate and `open_approvals`; a live `caught_up` ends the catch-up; every message write is recorded as `message.added`, `message.updated` or `message.deleted`.
- **Device-hosted tools and the device-tools grant.** A key's policy gains `device_tools`, the device labels (for example `["kai"]`) whose hosted tools it reaches; the tool scope then filters them like any server's. An allow pattern such as `kai__*` no longer reaches a device by itself (the upgrade grants the labels existing patterns named). A Chat thread's attached label that offers nothing says why in the error frame (`tool_unreachable`, `tool_offline`, ...).
- **Decision models.** `POST /v1/systemone` relays the System One wire (a state and typed questions, answered with calibrated probabilities) to a local llama.cpp decision model (b11361 or later) or to an OpenAI-compatible upstream such as OpenRouter. A GGUF whose header declares `decision.type` is a third aux kind, published as `decide/<id>`; aux rows gain `ubatch_size`, `batch_size`, `mmproj_path`, `backend` and `threads`. OpenRouter's decision, embedding, rerank, speech and image models now appear in `/v1/models` under their own tasks.
- **The lab store and the Decision lab.** The Decision, Image and Audio labs keep their runs in lmgw's database. The new Decision lab asks a decision model typed questions, compares and perturbs inputs, and saves question sets with a confidence threshold per question. A set run sends a CSV or JSONL file through a set as a job and reports accuracy, a confusion matrix, reliability bins and the threshold curve; batch agents can classify through a set. The Image and Audio labs save the files their runs made (one file, or a zip with a manifest).
- **Save As dialogs.** Every download in the desktop app asks where to save, through the desktop portal where there is one.
- **VRAM and plan accuracy.** A chat or aux row's footprint charges llama.cpp's compute buffers, and the KV cache follows llama.cpp's layout (sliding windows, shared layers, no V cache under MLA, MTP and draft contexts). A plan that cannot fit the card says so, and plans load nothing.
- **GGUF licence badges.** The Models page shows each file's licence from its header beside the row.
- **MIT licence.** lmgw was FSL-1.1-MIT; it is plain MIT now.

**Breaking / upgrade notes**

- **Paired devices must pair again.** Every existing device row becomes v1: its bearer opens nothing, and the refusal says so. Pair again from the Devices card and confirm the code; v1 pairing links are refused. `key_rotate` refuses a device.
- **Kai needs 0.2.0**, which pairs over the device link. Kai mobile 0.1.0 is released alongside.
- **VRAM estimates rise** for chat and aux rows (compute buffers), so admission can refuse or evict where a start used to fit.
- **Removed spellings are refused, naming the valid one:** the op `embed_model_set` (use `aux_model_set`); `embed` as an aux `target` (use `aux`); `upstream_set` protocol `openai` with kind `llama_server` (use `llama_cpp`); the `probe` parameter of the model plan tools.
- **Run arguments are lists of strings** (`extra_run_args`, `extra_args`) on every tool, op and answer; the newline or shell text form is refused.
- **Answers changed:** `key_create` answers `key` (was `plaintext`); `routable` is `routable_candidates`; unknown values are left out instead of `""` or `null`; unknown ids are `404 not_found` on the docs routes; a failed dictation answers `{code, message}`; the self-admin tools use the dashboard's names and types.
- Migrations 0079 to 0084 run on start. Building needs `opus-devel`; the RPM depends on `opus`.

**Fixes**

- Container starts no longer pass the desktop app's open files or `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` to `pasta`, which caused SELinux denials.
- A failed agent run no longer keeps the agent's token in its error text.
- Saving an alias no longer resets its min-p, repeat, presence and frequency penalties.
- Price sync leaves models billed per character, second or image unpriced instead of pricing them wrong.
- The Audio lab's voice list starts no model when the page opens.
- A voice-mode reply bubble stops spinning when its done frame is bad.
name: lmgw 0.5.0

body:
lmgw's own HTTP API is documented and typed, and a developer document covers what clients, devices and agents can call.

- **`/v1/openapi.json` is the developer document.** It lists every operation a non-owner credential reaches: the inference routes, the Chat API that paired devices use, the agent run API, and `GET /api/version`, with a map of which key kind may call what. The owner's admin plane stays in `/api/openapi.json`.
- **Documented for the first time:**
  - the rest of the Chat API: thread create, read, settings, delete, pin, move, archive and keep; send, continue, regenerate and edit with their SSE frames; message delete, read-aloud, voice warm-up, speech stop, search, folder patch and delete, attachments, and the exports (including the `lmgw.chat.v1` bundle);
  - the Knowledge bases API, the Audio lab and Image lab APIs, and `GET /chat/api/threads/rows`.

  Only the dashboard's pages, the `/ui` redirects and the agent app and MCP proxies stay undocumented.
- **Typed answers.** Every answer, op result and SSE frame of lmgw's own API is an `lmgw-api-types` type that the handler builds, and the schema comes from that type. Fields the server always sends are listed as `required`; request bodies of shared types are `<Name>Input` components. audio.cpp's own JSON (`/v1/tasks/*`, `/v1/audio/alignments`) is relayed verbatim and documented as such. The `/v1` protocol routes still pass unknown request parameters to the upstream.
- **Kept honest by tests.** Every drift test validates the live answer against the built document, including every Chat turn frame and the `/v1/chat/completions` stream. A test refuses new untyped answers, and a check holds the count of inline JSON in handlers and ops to a ratchet (README, "Typed answers").
- **Behaviour changes, malformed input and error paths only:**
  - A JSON body of the wrong shape is `422 bad_request` on every Chat route (send's `voice`, continue, regenerate and the job answer were 400). Invalid JSON stays 400.
  - Audio lab bodies of the wrong shape are `422 {error}`. Before, a non-string `transcript` cleared the clip's transcript and a non-string `alias` fell back to another model.
  - `GET /audio-lab/api/refs/{name}` errors are JSON `{error}` (were plain text). The Audio lab's speech and task hand-offs answer a bad body in the OpenAI envelope. Image lab errors gain `param`, `type` and `code` where they lacked them.
- **Fixes:** a tool turn could overflow a 2 MiB stack in a debug build; GitHub CI runs the full test suite again.
name: lmgw 0.4.4

body:
Personality profiles, approvals and late results for MCP tools, and client devices that host tools of their own.

- **Personality profiles.** A profile bundles a system prompt, reasoning settings and a voice, and shapes a thread's turns.
  - Assign one to a thread or a folder's defaults; the `chat_profile` setting names the Chat's profile for new threads. A folder with no profile inherits the Chat's; it does not mean "none". A spoken session follows its thread's profile from the next response.
  - Edit them at `/chat/profiles` (also Settings → Chat profile), with a drawer and folder picker, header chip and voice-panel chip in the Chat. Preview, voice Test and Speak work on an unsaved draft; a built-in profile can be reset. Unsaved edits ask before another profile opens, and Discard on a new profile drops the draft.
  - The self-admin tools `lmgw__profiles`, `lmgw__profile_set` and `lmgw__profile_delete` manage them. A device may change a profile that steers the admin tools only while it may write with them (`403 profile_in_admin_use`), and a device's TTS alias is checked against its key's scope.
- **Approvals for MCP tools.** `require_approval` on a thread (or folder default) stops a turn at a gated call.
  - The thread reports `pending_approvals`; `POST /chat/api/threads/{id}/approvals` decides, and the resumed reply streams on as its starter. A new message declines what waits. `approval.requested` and `approval.decided` events on the feed, the tool frame and the realtime `mcp_approval_*` items carry the call's `call_id`.
  - The dashboard shows Approve and Decline on the call's card, per card or as a batch.
  - A device can only tighten the rules: a write that gates fewer calls is `403 approval_loosen_refused`, and it decides only within its own reach (`approval_out_of_scope`). The owner's approval floor per thread and folder always holds, under either spelling of a tool's name.
- **Late tool results (MCP Tasks).** An MCP server that answers a tool call with a task no longer holds the turn.
  - The result enters the thread when it arrives, as an `lmgw__job_result` pair placed in chronological order, never while a turn runs, and a send, edit or regenerate keeps it.
  - `GET /chat/api/threads/{id}/tasks` lists a thread's jobs, `POST /chat/api/threads/{id}/tasks/{task}/cancel` cancels one, and `POST /chat/api/threads/{id}/answer` lets the model answer results that arrived while nobody was talking.
  - Bound voice sessions hear `lmgw.task.done` and the continuation is spoken. The dashboard shows a card (Job · tool · status) and a strip of the thread's jobs with Cancel; the server list counts open tasks (`open_tasks` on `GET /api/mcp-servers`).
  - `device.revoked` is a stored feed event for a deleted paired device, so a host can cancel the jobs that device started. A disable says nothing.
- **Devices host MCP tools.** A paired device can serve tools over `GET /mcp/host`; `initialize` tells it the link's limits (`lmgw/host_limits` in `_meta`). Closes say why (a deleted key is 4003; of two links the newer stays). A run calls only the tools it was offered. The dashboard's reach list shows a device chip.
- **`/mcp` passes resources through**, namespaced by tool prefix, with MCP Apps metadata: `tools/list` stamps each tool with `_meta["lmgw/server"]`, and the Chat tool frame gains `server_label`, `ui_resource` and `structured_content`. App-only tools stay out of model runs.
- **Colliding tool names no longer shadow each other.** Both tools move to `<server>__<tool>` (the server's own name still goes upstream; the frame says `tool_moved`), stable across restarts. A key's deny list holds under every name a tool has; an allow list admits only the name it names; a built-in's switch does not reach a server's tool.
- **`structuredContent` stays out of the model** when a result also has text content: clients and app views get it, the model reads the text.
- **Gemini tool loops keep their thought signatures.** The signature rides in the call's id and goes back to Gemini; an unsigned step gets the skip value. Chat completions, Messages and `/v1/responses` all pass it.
- **Fixes.**
  - The Chat page follows results stored before its own send in place, without a reload.
  - Test flakes were fixed (a Stop sent before a start, the VRAM sampler, realtime and agent waits); `scripts/flake-hunt.sh` runs the suite under load.
  - The self-update code moved into the `lmgw-update` crate; the feed's auth header goes only to the feed's own origin.

Upgrading: migrations 0071 to 0078 run on start (profiles, device MCP rows, tasks, pending approvals, a message's task, the approval floor, a message role index, known tools). Tools whose names collided are now prefixed by their server, so clients that called the bare name of the shadowed tool should list tools again.
name: lmgw 0.4.3

body:
Client apps as paired devices, prices beyond tokens, and a Chat that follows every client.

- **Client apps as paired devices.** Pair a client (a desktop voice client first, a phone later) from Usage → Keys → Devices with an `lmgw-pair:` link.
  - Each device gets its own key, tool scope and budget. It reaches the Chat API and `/v1`, and nothing of the admin plane.
  - Disable, Rotate and Delete end its connections at once. The realtime close says why: 4003 with a kind token for a revocation, 4004 for a thread out of reach.
  - A device can be given its own level of lmgw's admin tools (off, read only or full), capped by the gateway's own setting.
- **A Chat change feed and ongoing folders.** `GET /chat/api/feed` streams thread and folder changes, running turns, voice sessions and the GPU hold, and resumes across restarts.
  - A folder can be one ongoing conversation that every client continues (`POST /chat/api/folders/{id}/current`). A new thread starts after the folder's idle time or on "New conversation".
  - The new `lmgw-client` crate holds the realtime protocol, the voice state and the feed reader for clients; the dashboard's voice panel runs on it.
- **The dashboard's Chat follows other clients live.** A `chat` frame on `/api/events` names what changed, and the page reads it again without leaving the tab. A draft whose conversation was deleted elsewhere waits, unsaved, until you send it.
- **Prices beyond tokens.** A model can be priced per audio minute, per 1M characters, per generated image and per request, beside its token rates.
  - Requests record the audio length, characters and images they measured. Nothing is estimated: a quantity lmgw can't measure stays unknown, never 0.
  - Usage and Traffic show the quantities.
  - The catalog sync brings in request fees and cache prices, and a fallback is priced as the alias that answered.
- **Supertonic speaks typographic text.** A reply containing a character the model's vocabulary lacks, such as „ or an emoji, no longer fails its speech. Such characters become plain equivalents or are dropped, and `x-lmgw-speech` names them. A text with nothing left to say is `empty_input` on every TTS model.
- **No more "database is locked".** Every write takes SQLite's write lock up front, so concurrent writes wait their turn instead of failing.
- **MCP servers connect or fail.** An HTTP/SSE server's handshake is bounded by its `timeout_ms`.
  - Podman-isolated servers run in labelled containers, which are removed when the server stops and swept at the next start.
  - Settings saves and the GPU hold no longer wait for MCP reconnects.
- **Streams follow `stream_options.include_usage`.** Streamed chat completions end with a usage chunk only when the client asks for it, as OpenAI's do.
- **A clean shutdown.** Quit, an update's restart and SIGTERM stop the gateway first: feeds and voice sessions close with 1001, and cut turns keep their partial reply.
- **The API reference reads as documentation for client developers.**

Upgrading: migrations 0061 to 0070 run on start. If an old price row used a removed unit (`per_second`, `per_char`), lmgw refuses to start and names the row. Delete it and enter the price again in the new units. Run the price sync once after upgrading, so request fees and cache prices arrive.
name: lmgw 0.4.2

body:
Tools in voice conversations, llama.cpp as a backend of its own, and an app window that feels native.

- **Tools in voice conversations.** A `/v1/realtime` session can offer MCP tools the way OpenAI's Realtime API does (`{"type": "mcp"}`): lmgw runs the calls on its own MCP servers, by label, and reports them as `mcp_call` items; the client sends the follow-up. `GET /v1/mcp/servers` and `/v1/mcp/servers/{label}` list the servers and their tools for a client's picker. `/v1/responses` now takes `allowed_tools` as `{tool_names: [...]}` too and refuses a malformed one instead of allowing every tool.
- **llama.cpp gets its own backend.** llama-server rows speak their own protocol (existing rows migrate on start): what a model can do comes from the server's `/props`, and images returned by tools reach a model that sees them. ik_llama.cpp rows use the same path.
- **Configured fallbacks always apply.** A fallback that cannot see gets placeholders for the images (a PDF's pages go as its text) instead of the request waiting for the local model, and the response header `x-lmgw-images-omitted` counts them. A voice turn goes as audio to whichever model answers if it hears audio, cloud and LAN models included (the setting is now off/on, a stored `local` reads as on); otherwise it goes as the transcript. Voice-clip transcription follows the configured fallback. The Traffic page marks every request whose content was reduced this way.
- **No orphaned model containers.** A client that hangs up while its model loads no longer leaves the container running unregistered, which used to block that model with `vram_queue_timeout`. After start, lmgw adopts or removes the containers it owns, and a request its client gave up on is logged as a 499 row.
- **A native app window on KDE.** KWin draws the frame, the app uses the desktop's fonts and the title bar's colours, the traffic pulse and the GPU status sit at the foot of the sidebar, right-click gives a desktop menu instead of a browser's, the window opens fully drawn, and the scrollbars are thin. The default interface scale is now 125%.
- **Browser clients with a gateway key.** CORS preflights now echo the requested headers, so a browser can send `Authorization`.

Download the RPM below and install it with `sudo dnf install ./lmgw-*.x86_64.rpm`, or let the app offer the update.
name: lmgw 0.4.1

body:
Voice: talk to your models, in the app and over the API.

- **Realtime voice API.** `/v1/realtime` speaks OpenAI's Realtime protocol over a WebSocket and answers with your own models: turn detection inside lmgw (Silero VAD, and Smart Turn for `semantic_vad`), speech to text, a chat model with tools, and text to speech. Interrupting cuts the answer, and the history keeps only what was heard.
- **Voice in the Chat.** Dictation into the composer, read-aloud of replies (code blocks and tables are announced, not read), and a voice mode that talks with the open thread. Choose the microphone and the output in the app. Each thread can have its own speech models, voice, style and languages: the language you speak and the one the reply is spoken in can differ. A local model that hears audio can get your voice turn as audio (a setting, off by default).
- **Natural speech output.** Replies go to text to speech in whole sentences, several to a request, and the silence an engine pads its audio with is capped by a new setting, Settings → Realtime → Longest pause.
- **Audio models.** Catalog downloads follow the revision a model's spec pins, a package can be completed in one go, and an audio model can run on the CPU with its own thread count, where it keeps serving while the GPU hold is on.
- Many fixes around audio containers, the GPU hold and the catalog.

Download the RPM below and install it with `sudo dnf install ./lmgw-*.x86_64.rpm`, or let the app offer the update. The README has the voice setup.
name: lmgw 0.4.0

body:
First public release.

lmgw, short for local model gateway, is a Linux desktop app. It runs models on your own GPU and serves them through local copies of the OpenAI and Anthropic APIs. Cloud providers sit behind the same aliases, picked by you or used as a fallback.

Download the RPM below and install it with `sudo dnf install ./lmgw-*.x86_64.rpm`. Requirements and a quick start are in the README. From now on the app checks this page itself and offers each new release.
name: lmgw 0.3.0
